Switching from Windows to Mac doesn't actually bring many software limitations. The platform can run most major computer applications, and there's a huge selection of useful Mac-exclusive apps to choose from.

The biggest exception is gaming. However, the latest tests show that, whether through official or unofficial means, Windows games currently perform better on Mac than ever before……

Apple has its own Game Porting Toolkit, which helps developers evaluate how their Windows games will run on Mac, with the goal of encouraging and facilitating the porting of games to the Mac platform.

However, as Macworld's Filipe Esposito points out, this toolkit has also been used by players to unofficially run Windows software on Mac—and he himself is one of them. He notes that the latest test version brings significant performance improvements, using GTA V as an example.

After testing the fourth beta version of the Game Porting Toolkit for several days on a MacBook Pro equipped with an M4 Pro chip, he found that these performance improvements essentially transformed the experience of running demanding Windows games……On the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, using the same in-game settings and benchmarks, the frame rate of GTA V increased from approximately 106 fps in the GPTK 3 era to approximately 176 fps in GPTK 4 beta, representing an increase of about 66%. The game ran quite smoothly at medium-to-high quality settings at 2K resolution.

He acknowledged that not every game would see such significant improvements, but he hoped these advances would encourage game developers to see Mac as a viable platform.
